title: Backend Developer
summary: Backend developers build the servers, APIs and databases that apps and websites depend on. The role suits students who like logic, data and making things reliable and secure, more than visual design.

nodes.title: One server-side language
nodes.summary: Pick one language such as Python, Java or JavaScript (Node.js) and learn it well, including its package manager and how to structure a project. Depth in one language matters more than a little of many.
nodes.proof: Build a small command-line tool, such as a task tracker that saves to a file, in your chosen language and publish it on GitHub.

sources.title: The 5 Best Backend Development Languages – roadmap.sh

nodes.title: Git, the terminal and Linux basics
nodes.summary: Servers are mostly run from a terminal. Learn shell commands, editing files, environment variables and Git for version control. These daily tools are rarely taught in class but expected at work.

resources.title: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education – MIT

nodes.proof: Write a shell script that sets up and runs one of your projects, and keep every project in Git with meaningful commits.

sources.title: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education – MIT

nodes.title: HTTP and REST API design
nodes.summary: Understand HTTP methods, status codes and headers, then learn to design clean REST APIs: resource URLs, versioning, pagination, error responses and rate limiting.

resources.title: Overview of HTTP – MDN Web Docs
HTTP request methods – MDN Web Docs

nodes.proof: Write an API design document for a small app listing each endpoint, its method, request body, responses and error codes.

nodes.title: A web framework
nodes.summary: Learn one framework for your language, for example Express for Node.js. Cover routing, middleware, request validation and structured error handling, and keep business logic separate from route handlers.

resources.title: Python Backend Development: Build Your First API – roadmap.sh

nodes.proof: Build the API you designed earlier, with input validation and consistent JSON error responses for bad requests.

nodes.title: Relational databases and SQL
nodes.summary: Learn to model data in tables, write queries with joins, use indexes to speed up searches, and use transactions. Also learn when a NoSQL store like MongoDB or a cache like Redis is a better fit.

resources.title: CS50's Introduction to Databases with SQL (archived, free to view)

nodes.proof: Design a normalised schema for a library or shop with at least four tables, and write ten queries including joins and an aggregate.

sources.title: CS50's Introduction to Databases with SQL

nodes.title: Authentication and API security
nodes.summary: Store passwords with a slow hash such as Argon2id, manage sessions or tokens safely, and check on every request that the user may access that exact record. Broken access control is the top web risk on the OWASP list.
nodes.proof: Add login to your API and write tests proving that one user gets a 403 or 404 when asking for another user's records.

nodes.title: Testing, containers and deployment
nodes.summary: Write automated tests for your API so you can change code without fear. Package the app and its database with Docker so it runs the same on any machine, then deploy it.
nodes.proof: Your API repo has a test suite you can run with one command and a Docker Compose file that starts the API and database together.

sources.title: Build and share a containerized application – Docker Docs

nodes.title: Caching, scaling and system design basics
nodes.summary: Learn the core ideas behind larger systems: caching, load balancing, replication, sharding and message queues, and the trade-offs between consistency and availability. Start with simple diagrams of systems you already use.
nodes.proof: Draw and explain a design for a URL shortener, covering storage, caching and what happens when traffic grows ten times.

nodes.title: Build a production-style API
nodes.summary: Build one realistic backend from start to finish, such as an e-commerce or booking API, with login, a database, tests, Docker and clear docs. This is the main thing you will talk about in interviews.

resources.title: Todo List API Project Idea – roadmap.sh

nodes.proof: A public repo with a deployed API, API documentation, passing tests and a README explaining your design decisions.

nodes.title: Interview preparation and applying
nodes.summary: Prepare to explain your project in depth, answer questions on databases, HTTP and security, and solve coding problems on data structures. Learn the usual hiring steps and apply steadily.

resources.title: Preparing to Interview and Interviewing – The Odin Project

nodes.proof: Give a ten-minute walkthrough of your project to a senior or friend, and keep a log of at least 75 solved coding problems.
